title: 版本化 pipeline adapter

review.note: Round 1 blocked on forged/unbound cache metadata and un-evictable poisoned entries; both fixed and independently reproduced. Round 2 accepted: metadata bound to stage kind/execution/provider/model/prompt/rule-pack, cache hits report cached:true, invalid entries are deleted and rewritten, repeated poison fails INTERNAL_ERROR. 14/14 scenarios; regressions V6-10 36, V6-14 41, V6-15 41, tsc and build exit 0. Node 22 remains unverified; C11 checkpoint schema/ownership and canonical per-stage consent scope remain NEEDS_DECISION.

interface.usage: Construct with the existing LLMProvider, provider/model ids, purpose, stageVersion, PipelineOptions, and an authorize callback for provider mode; call run(context, targetStage). The returned PipelineAdapterResult contains a cloned PipelineContext and testOutput flag. An optional cache scope and cache implementation support caller-managed namespaced checkpoint storage.
interface.cache: SHA-256 of canonical NFC JSON over stage, stageVersion, provider/model, prompt/rule versions, effective input, project/cache scope, and upstream output hashes. Cache metadata is bound to the active mode and versions; untrusted entries are deleted before recomputation. Cache hits set meta.cached=true, including restored upstream checkpoints.
interface.authorization: Before every real LLMProvider.generateStructured invocation, authorize receives stage, effective-scope hash, provider id, model id, and purpose. A refusal or missing authorizer throws PipelineAdapterError with the contract error code before the provider is called. Stub mode bypasses authorization and the injected provider and marks testOutput=true.
interface.failure: PipelineAdapterError exposes code and stage; provider errors preserve providerCode and map to contract-oriented codes. Failed stages are not cached; successful checkpoints remain reusable. The adapter blocks PipelineRunner's schema-repair request before it reaches the injected provider, so a schema-invalid first response fails immediately as PROVIDER_SCHEMA_INVALID.
interface.purity: run clones caller input, validates cached schema/hash data before reuse, and uses injected clock/cache/provider/authorization dependencies. No default provider call or network invocation was made during implementation or tests.

acceptance.observed: 14 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Identical input resumes with cached metadata, including restored upstream checkpoints; changed chunk facts and user answers invalidate affected stages while independent branches remain cached; provider/model/prompt/rule-pack/stage version variants miss. Stub outputs carry model=null and testOutput=true. Forged metadata is rejected. The poisoned-hash probe made 1 provider call and 1 cache rewrite for the rejected stage; the following adapter made 0 provider calls and 0 cache writes, and reused the repaired entry. The schema failure made exactly one provider call, preserved prior checkpoints, omitted the failed checkpoint, and succeeded after correction.

Authorization refusal returns RELEASE_GATE_CLOSED with zero provider calls. Stub makes zero injected-provider calls, sets model=null, and marks testOutput=true. Changed input uses distinct cache keys; forged cache metadata is discarded and recomputed.

Concurrent and repeated snapshots do not duplicate provider calls/cache writes; general provider failure retains earlier checkpoints and retry reruns only failed and downstream stages; invalid cached hashes are deleted and repaired, then reused without duplicate provider calls; input remains unchanged.

runs.name: workspace regression
runs.observed: 15 worker tests and 44 export checks passed

specAcceptance.reason: The adapter tests that an injected authorization refusal returns RELEASE_GATE_CLOSED with zero provider calls, but it does not load ProviderProfile or render a disabled control for processingRegion=null. Profile completeness and UI state remain outside this library seam.

The adapter has no payload-manifest builder or consent scope model. It calculates an effective stage input scope hash but cannot prove a newly added file is excluded by a persisted Consent; V6-15 covers manifest and stale-consent behavior.
Quota accounting and platform-provider job creation are not part of this library adapter. No quota or provider fallback exists here; adapter never selects another provider.
Adapter checkpoints are in-memory or caller-cache entries, not R2 jobs; jobId persistence, refresh recovery and worker stage status are not represented.
No R2 worker, lease, owner or fencing token is modeled by this library adapter.
The adapter returns pipeline context and does not create/adopt a generation Job or set obsolete_result. It does invalidate cache entries when input changes, but cannot enact draft adoption semantics.
The adapter recognizes PipelineRunner’s deterministic #1 schema-repair request and fails with PROVIDER_SCHEMA_INVALID before a second provider call; the runner itself is unchanged.
specAcceptance.observed: A schema-invalid first response yields PROVIDER_SCHEMA_INVALID after exactly one provider call; earlier checkpoint retained; failed stage absent from cache; corrected retry succeeds.

specAcceptance.reason: The callback is checked before each real provider invocation and can return CONSENT_REVOKED, but revocation state, in-flight job transition and UI notice are outside the adapter's contract. No revoked-consent integration was claimed.

The adapter does not own page lifecycle or persistent R1 interruption state. A caller-provided persistent cache could resume data, but interrupted status and refreshed authorization flow are not implemented here.
No invocation-record or UI/network response projection exists in this library adapter; this ticket cannot demonstrate DOM or response content redaction.

limitations: No real provider, model, network, credential or customer-material call was made; tests use synthetic fixtures and counting mock providers only.
Library-level adapter only. No route, UI, job row, quota, persistent worker, lease/fencing, draft adoption, or actual consent repository integration is implemented.

Default MemoryPipelineStageCache lasts only for the adapter instance. A durable checkpoint store can implement PipelineStageCache, but no IndexedDB checkpoint schema or storage ownership contract is defined here.
Stage versions are supplied by the caller as one stageVersion string; no per-stage version registry is defined by this ticket's contracts.

Cache records validate output hashes, active provider/model or stub metadata, prompt/rule versions, and all embedded upstream checkpoint metadata. Malformed entries are deleted before recomputation; retained poisoned values are retried once and then fail INTERNAL_ERROR.
Evidence commands ran on Node 25.8.1. The architecture note specifies Node 22; Node 22 was not available and is unverified.
The adapter intercepts PipelineRunner's schema-repair request and fails immediately before it reaches the injected provider. The runner implementation is unchanged.
The production build passed with Vite's existing warning that some minified chunks exceed 500 kB.

decisionsRequested.question: What IndexedDB checkpoint object-store schema, ownership key, and retention/cleanup policy should implement the persistence required by C11?
decisionsRequested.suggestion: Specify the IndexedDB checkpoint object-store shape, key fields, actor/tenant/matter/target ownership checks, and retention/cleanup policy for the cache implementation.
decisionsRequested.impact: Persistence is required by C11; this ticket exposes and validates a cache seam but cannot define its durable storage schema or ownership rules without contract guidance.

decisionsRequested.question: Which canonical scope object must the consent authorizer validate for each stage, including derived upstream outputs?
decisionsRequested.suggestion: Define a versioned stage payload manifest that binds source/assets/facts/draft/figures and the exact stage input before integration with validateConsentForUse.
decisionsRequested.impact: The adapter supplies an effective-input/upstream scope hash but cannot assert it is equivalent to ConsentScope.payloadManifestHash.
